string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People’s Republic of China and one of the most populous cities in the world, with more than 20 million residents. Located in the north of the country, it has long served as a political, cultural, and educational centre. The city is renowned for landmarks such as the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven, and the Great Wall, which stretches across the mountains just beyond its northern edge. Beijing hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics and the 2022 Winter Olympics, becoming the first city to stage both events. Today it blends imperial history with modern skyscrapers and a rapidly growing technology industry.

Shanghai is China’s largest city by population and one of the world’s leading financial and commercial centres. Situated on the east coast at the mouth of the Yangtze River, it is a major international port and a global hub for trade, finance, and innovation. The city is famous for its distinctive skyline along the Bund and the towering skyscrapers of Pudong, including the Shanghai Tower. Shanghai combines modern prosperity with a rich cultural heritage reflected in its museums, classical gardens, and historic lanes. It is also a centre of education and manufacturing and attracts millions of visitors every year.

Chongqing is a major city in southwest China and one of the country’s four municipalities directly administered by the central government. Situated at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers, it is a key inland transport and manufacturing hub. With an enormous administrative area and a population of over 30 million, it ranks among the largest cities in the world. Chongqing is known for its mountainous, hilly landscape, its hot and spicy cuisine, especially the local hotpot, and its dramatic night views along the rivers. In recent decades it has grown rapidly as a gateway to western China.

Tianjin is a major coastal city in northern China and one of the country’s four municipalities under direct central administration. Located southeast of Beijing on the Bohai Sea, it serves as an important seaport and a centre of industry and commerce. The city has a long history of trade and is known for its distinctive blend of Chinese and Western architecture, particularly in its former foreign concession districts. Tianjin is also a hub for manufacturing, finance, and logistics. Notable landmarks include the Tianjin Eye, a large Ferris wheel built over the Hai River, and the Ancient Culture Street.
